title: Lahaina Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: February 21, 2024

issues.title: Moving fire survivors off FEMA interim housing

recap.headline: Lahaina recovery update: debris removal, cesspool guidance and disposal site survey
recap.in_60_seconds: County, state and federal recovery officials held their weekly Lahaina update to report on debris removal, water and sewer testing, health studies and the permanent debris disposal site survey. Thirteen residents asked questions, many about new Department of Health guidance letting burned Wahikuli homes keep their cesspools. The Corps of Engineers said debris work has reached 149 properties, with 15 fully completed. The County said more than 2,700 survey responses will re-weight its criteria, with a site decision on or before March 1. Residents' questions on engineer costs, testing of unscraped yard areas, FEMA housing delays and rebuild permitting were left partly unanswered or set for follow-up.

parts.title: Opening and updates from the Mayor and Council member
presented: Free pet and adult supply packs offered at the Lahaina Pet Resource Center and Maui Seaside.
The County asked the Legislature's Ways and Means Committee for $401.75 million for infrastructure, housing and emergency preparation, with about $198.75 million in County money, over three years.
The U.S. Transportation Secretary visited; realigning Honoapiʻilani Highway between Ukumehame and Olowalu was discussed.
The State Department of Human Services will hold a meeting on interim housing for FEMA-ineligible survivors.

next.what: State DHS meeting on interim housing for FEMA-ineligible survivors at the Lahaina Civic Center gym

parts.title: Ola Lahaina online engagement for recovery planning
parts.presenter: Administrator, County Long Range Planning Division
presented: New Ola Lahaina website at MauiRecovers.org/Lahaina collects views on Lahaina's strengths and weaknesses.
Input will help draft Lahaina's long-term recovery plan.
Planners are at the Disaster Recovery Center Tuesday to Thursday, 9 to 3 this month.

next.what: In-person planning table moves to Wednesdays only, 9 to 3

parts.title: Debris removal update from the Corps of Engineers
presented: The temporary debris storage site is working as designed; rainwater that passes through debris is captured and treated.
Under Bill 120, testing covers water after every 1-inch-or-greater rain, runoff and air, with two new monitoring wells uphill and downhill.
Debris work has reached 149 properties; 134 are cleared and 15 are fully complete with clearance letters returned to the County.
The commander leaves next week after six months; his replacement was introduced.

parts.title: A homeowner's debris removal experience
parts.presenter: Member of the Mayor's Lahaina advisory team
presented: His family's lot was cleared in about two days by a five-person crew with local roots.
He praised air, ash and truck monitoring and safety.
He is now waiting for soil test results, gravel for erosion control and County clearance to apply for permits.

parts.title: EPA drinking water and sewer work
presented: 118 fire hydrants sampled for chlorine, bacteria and chemicals; service line sampling is next.
Contaminated service lines will be capped, and the County will replace them later.
Sewer cleaning and camera inspection began February 5; video is reviewed by the County.
Night sewer work along the highway near Safeway and the Civic Center is expected to take about a week.

next.what: Night sewer inspection work with possible traffic, noise and lights

parts.title: Department of Health air, cesspool and health study update
presented: 51 air sensors and 4 air samplers operate around Lahaina and Olowalu; January 13 to 24 tests showed good air and no asbestos.
Burned Wahikuli homes may keep using cesspools while a sewer is planned, about 3 to 5 years out, if an engineer certifies them and bedrooms match pre-fire records.
Lead screening has found few elevated levels; a report will follow.
University of Hawaiʻi wildfire exposure study offers a $100 gift card and lead screening.

next.what: Cesspool guidance posted online and given to the County
Exposure study recruitment events: Royal Lahaina, Lahaina Civic Center and Ritz-Carlton Kapalua
next.when: Friday 3 to 7 p.m., Saturday 10 to 4, Sunday 10 to 2

parts.title: Permanent debris disposal site survey results
parts.presenter: County Department of Environmental Management deputy director and recovery outreach staff
presented: About 430 people answered a scientific random survey and 2,327 an open public survey.
About 56% of public respondents were from West Maui, 78% were lifelong or 20-plus-year residents, and 49% were directly affected.
About 8 in 10 rated distance from the environment and homes or schools 9 or 10; about 5 in 10 rated logistics that high.
The department will re-weight its criteria, lowering time-to-ready, and choose among three sites.

parts.title: Questions for the Department of Health

raised.concern: Owners must pay for an engineer to certify cesspools, which many cannot afford; they asked whether a plumber would do and whether a recovery fund could pay.
Requiring the same number of bedrooms limits underinsured families who need to rebuild for multiple generations.
Yard areas outside the Corps scrape zone may still hold wind-blown ash; will anyone test or clear them, and is bioremediation recommended?
What erosion control is used, where the cinder comes from, and how long soil testing takes.

answered.said: A civil engineer must certify the cesspool; a certified plumber or civil engineer can certify the home connection.
Engineers advise a licensed engineer is needed, but she will take the question back to staff.
The department does not sample yards; homeowners do, and the department can help analyze results. She would rely on Corps sampling of the debris field.
Bedrooms are checked against permits and tax records so cesspools do not overflow; a smaller modular home first is allowed.
Gravel or crushed cinder is used only for erosion control; tests take 7 to 10 days; cinder is not necessarily from Olowalu.

next.what: Department of Health to review whether a plumber can certify instead of an engineer

raised.concern: Where can owners who opt out take debris from their own cleanup?
How the three disposal sites ranked in the survey.
Mental health needs and traffic in West Maui.
FEMA direct lease homes held with landlords paid while families wait months with no callback; at least 20 households affected.
Rents have nearly doubled and FEMA requires three housing searches a month.
How to see where a property is in the debris removal queue and speed it up.
The ash holds memories and lost lives; the disposal site should be a place of honor, a Lahaina lookout, not a dump.
Why debris removal on one street skipped some lots.
When owners can rebuild and how to speed permitting; a County press release on contractor placards caused confusion.

answered.said: Only Corps contractors may use the temporary site; one rebuild project used the Central Maui Landfill under strict Department of Health rules, which the Department of Health can explain.
An update for owners who opted out will come at next week's or the following meeting.
The survey rated criteria, not sites; the department director will explain the final ranking next week.
Traffic will be covered next week with County Public Works and state highways staff.
Asked if the family used the helpline and offered individual follow-up after the meeting.
Acknowledged Maui's housing inventory is very challenging.
Archaeologists and cultural monitors must clear each property after the County sends the right of entry; he will look up the address.
Only ash and debris go to the storage site; metal and concrete are recycled first.
The first 268 rights of entry started the contract, so early work looks patchy; the rest have since been added.

answered.who: Administrator, County Long Range Planning Division
answered.said: A consultant is being hired for simple permits outside special areas; small SMA projects may self-certify for exemption; flood permits remain under federal law.

next.what: Environmental Management director to present the final site decision

parts.title: Mayor's closing remarks on rebuilding
presented: The County will bring its expedited permitting team to a future meeting.
Rebuilding depends on water, sewer and power; parts of Kahoma appear ready.
Narrow roads may need widening, and voluntary land swaps for mauka lots are being explored, not eminent domain.

answered.said: Building depends on infrastructure and location; shoreline and road decisions must come first, and he asked residents to be open to compromise.

next.what: Expedited permitting team to attend a meeting

bills.name: Bill 120
bills.what: County law passed in January setting environmental testing and monitoring for the temporary debris storage site.

bills.name: Lahaina long-term recovery plan
bills.what: Plan for Lahaina's wildfire recovery to be drafted with community input from Ola Lahaina.

open_questions.question: Can a licensed plumber certify cesspools instead of an engineer, and will any fund pay for certification?
Will anyone test or clear yard areas outside the Corps scrape zone?
What rules apply to owners who clean up their own debris, and where can they take it?
Why are FEMA direct lease homes sitting empty while matched families wait?
When can owners on cleared lots start rebuilding?

not_on_tracker.topic: Cesspool rules for rebuilding burned Wahikuli homes
not_on_tracker.why: Engineer costs and bedroom limits affect whether families can afford to rebuild the homes they need.
West Maui residents care deeply where the ash of their town and lost loved ones will rest.

not_on_tracker.topic: Debris removal order and testing of unscraped yards
not_on_tracker.why: Owners want to know when their lots will be cleared and whether yards where children play are safe.
Survivors face rents nearly double what they paid before the fire.
Owners are unsure when they may build and were confused by a County announcement.

moments.quote: So there's discussion of some monies we've received from the federal government and from other sources, other partners, to try to realign that road so we can improve access in and out of Lahaina.
moments.about: Says federal and partner money is being pursued to realign Honoapiʻilani Highway between Ukumehame and Olowalu to improve Lahaina access.

moments.who: County Planning Department Long Range Planning Division administrator
moments.quote: ʻOla Lahaina will be the main resource for staying informed on the latest in-person and online engagement events, accessing feedback from fellow community members and contributing to drafting Lahaina's long-term recovery plan.
moments.about: Introduces the Ola Lahaina website as the main way residents can help shape the Lahaina long-term recovery plan.

moments.who: County Planning Department Long Range Planning Division administrator
moments.quote: We are here three days a week for this month. Starting March 1st, we'll be here on Wednesdays from 9 to 3. So please come and visit us.
moments.about: Gives in-person times at the Disaster Recovery Center for residents to give input on the long-term recovery plan.

moments.quote: If you haven't yet heard about this study, this is being run by the University of Hawaiʻi, and they're doing a pretty extensive look and evaluation to see how people have been impacted by the fires in August.
moments.about: Explains that the University of Hawaiʻi is running the Maui wildfire exposure study and is still recruiting participants.

moments.quote: But it is very reassuring at this time that people are not having heavy contamination exposures from the ash. Still want everyone to be careful.
moments.about: Shares early lead screening results, done alongside study recruitment, showing few signs of heavy ash exposure.
